name: Bún cá Ninh Hòa
summary: A fish noodle bowl from Ninh Hòa that the provincial page also puts on tables in Nha Trang. The body text and the caption name different fish for the pulled meat. Both lists stay. The page says people eat it in the morning and again in the evening.
origin: Ninh Hòa. The same page says visitors look for the bowl in Nha Trang and does not name a street there.
history: The provincial page reprints a Báo Khánh Hòa story from May 2026. It calls bún cá a Ninh Hòa bowl and a Khánh Hòa specialty eaten in Nha Trang.
texture: Fish is steamed, bones removed, and pulled into pieces the page calls cá dầm. The fish cake is fried or steamed after the flesh is pounded until it holds.
howToEat: The page says the broth is fish bone, simmered for hours, with a little pineapple and tomato.
Add herbs cut thin, rau thơm, bean sprouts, and banana blossom. The page says a squeeze of lime, a little chili fish sauce, and a few slices of chili.
The body text says the pulled fish is cá thu, cá ngừ, and cá cờ. The caption says cá dầm is usually made from cá bò and cá ngừ. The cake is from cá đỏ, cá nhồng, and cá thu ảo.
where: Ninh Hòa for the origin. In Nha Trang the page does not name a shop or a street. Chợ Đầm’s market page names bún cá inside the hall, without a stall number.
No shop price was printed. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Bún cá Ninh Hòa — the Nha Trang fish bowl
seoDescription: The provincial page’s bún cá: two fish lists, a clear broth, and a fish cake. Eaten morning and evening. No Nha Trang street was printed.
